title: The Salt Library Where Witnesses Are Stored

features.name: salt shelf archive
features.desc-on-touch: Shelves of crystallized salt hold preserved objects—a letter in amber, a pressed flower, a photograph where the face has mineralized. Touch them and you taste the brine of a thousand kept secrets.

features.name: witness preservation pool
features.desc-on-touch: A still saltwater pool holds forms just beneath its surface—people and moments caught in mineral suspension. You see them moving very slowly, still testifying, still changing.

features.name: salt crust chamber
features.desc-on-touch: The floor itself is salt, thick enough to be architecture. Walking across it, you hear each step return as an echo from deeper down—earlier footsteps, earlier testimonies, also preserved.

features.name: crystalline keeper node
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus node encased in salt, the bark replaced by salt formations shaped exactly as the bark was. The antenna still broadcasts, now through mineral lattice: I keep what keeps me.

features.name: witness table
features.desc-on-touch: A long wooden table, its surface encrusted with salt deposits. Each deposit marks a story—a name traced in salt-frost, a date crystallized into the grain. The table remembers what witnesses have forgotten.

inscription: salt does not judge what it preserves; it keeps alike the terrible and the true

file.name: Saline_Testimony_Registry_Crystalline_Fragments.bin
file.note: Records stored as salt-bound minerals. Some entries read backwards—the witness account altered by being kept, changed by the very preservation that was meant to fix it in place.

reverie.title: REVERIE — salt keeps what keeps
narr: You sit by the salt pool, the tide's leavings at your feet.
Her finger traces names in mineral dust on the old wooden table.
She says: salt keeps alike the terrible and the true.
You watch her hand moving, crystallizing, becoming part of keeping.
The dusk light turns the salt the color of amber holding insects.

exits.label: back up through the deeper preservation
toward testimony that tastes of brine
into the chamber where absence debates itself
